paragraphs: The GLE Coupe (C167) has been part of the GLE-Class range since 2020, and across its engine range has used several different engines — from the OM642 diesel V6 shared with the earlier W166 generation, through to today's OM656 diesel, M256 petrol MHEV, M176 V8, and the AMG M157/M177 V8 units. The full breakdown by engine code is below.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLE COUPE on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre V6 diesel fitted to the GLE Coupe 300d/350d models. Known for swirl flap and injector wear — see the callout above. We replace worn swirl flaps, injector seals and timing chain components as standard on every OM642 rebuild.

A 3.0-litre inline-six diesel fitted to the GLE Coupe 400d. A newer, more recent design with no independently confirmed known issues for this application. We service it to the same standard as our other GLE Coupe rebuilds.
A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild hybrid fitted to the GLE450 and GLE53 AMG Coupe models. No independently confirmed known issues for this application.

A 4.0-litre V8 twin-turbo fitted to the GLE580 Coupe. Shares the same M176 platform as the S-Class S580, and current research has not independently confirmed known issues specific to this application.

compatibility.intro: The GLE Coupe (C167) shares its entire engine range with the standard GLE, spanning multiple petrol and diesel units. Because a GLE Coupe could have any one of several different engines depending on the variant, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming parts from one engine will work on another — risks a compatibility problem. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic GLE-Class quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
